title: Elodie and the Summer
premise: Elodie Marchand, a restorer of old photographs, arrives at the failing Almeida vineyard to catalog an estate being seized for debt, only to find Sebastian Almeida — the man she loved and lost a decade ago — drowning in creditors and pride. When a freak June snowstorm strands them alongside Camille Roux, the rival winemaker who was the other half of their shared history, old betrayals resurface: Camille holds the loan that could save or destroy the vineyard, and Elodie discovers the 'betrayal' that ended her romance was engineered to protect her. As harvest approaches, Elodie must choose between returning to her ordered life in Lyon or staying past the last train, betting on a man learning that justice sometimes means forgiving what the law would punish. The novel ends at the first harvest festival, where Sebastian signs the vineyard over to a cooperative rather than surrender it to Camille's bank, and Elodie unpacks her suitcase for good.
about_author: Odile Villalobos is a former archivist from Valparaíso who writes love stories set among things people refuse to throw away. She splits her year between Chilean coastal towns and borrowed kitchens in the French countryside, where most of her novels are drafted by hand.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Elodie arrives at Château Almeida to appraise its contents for the court-ordered liquidation, camera bag in hand. POV: Elodie. She catalogs dusty cellars and faded family portraits, then freezes: a photograph of herself, age twenty-four, still framed on Sebastian's desk. Beat: dread mixed with the ache of unfinished business.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Debts
chapters.summary: Sebastian returns from a humiliating meeting with the bank and finds a stranger photographing his mother's portrait — until he recognizes her. POV: Sebastian. Ten years of silence collapse into one hostile, electric conversation. He orders her off the property; she refuses, citing her contract. Beat: wounded pride masking longing.

chapters.title: What the Vine Remembers
chapters.summary: Working through the estate, Elodie finds ledgers showing Sebastian has quietly paid his workers' wages before his own debts for three years. POV: Elodie. Her contempt softens into curiosity about the man he became. A storm warning crackles on the radio. Beat: reluctant admiration taking root.

chapters.title: Snow in June
chapters.summary: An impossible late-spring snowstorm closes the mountain road. Stranded overnight: Elodie, Sebastian, and — arriving soaked and furious — Camille Roux, the rival vintner whose bank holds the Almeida loan. POV: rotating close-third. Three enemies, one fireplace, no escape. Beat: claustrophobic tension with sparks of old intimacy.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Wine loosens tongues. Camille reveals she was there the night everything ended ten years ago, and Elodie learns Sebastian never sent the letter she waited for. POV: Elodie. Accusations fly; Sebastian walks out into the snow rather than explain. Beat: the wound reopened, wider than memory.

chapters.title: Camille's Version
chapters.summary: While Sebastian sleeps off the argument, Camille tells Elodie her side: she loved him too, and chose money over waiting. Now she offers Elodie a job in Lyon if she'll testify the inventory supports full liquidation. POV: Camille. Beat: sympathy curdling into manipulation; the reader sees Camille's loneliness beneath the armor.

chapters.title: Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: The roads clear. Camille leaves first; Elodie stays to finish the appraisal, telling herself it's professionalism. POV: Sebastian. He watches her work and finally explains the letter: his father intercepted it, threatening to disown him if he followed Elodie to Lyon. Beat: grief for the decade stolen from them both.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Elodie's appraisal is complete. At the station, ticket in hand, she hesitates as Sebastian asks her — plainly, without poetry — to stay until harvest. POV: Elodie. She boards anyway, then gets off at the next stop and calls him. Beat: the first true choice; terror and exhilaration.

chapters.title: Learning the Rows
chapters.summary: Elodie moves into the estate cottage and begins documenting the vineyard properly — not for the court, but for Sebastian. POV: alternating. Montage of small intimacies: pruning lessons, burned dinners, laughter startling them both. Beat: tentative joy, both waiting for it to be taken away.

chapters.title: Creditors at the Gate
chapters.summary: A bailiff posts seizure notices on the cellar doors. Sebastian's crew threatens to walk; Elodie uses her archival skills to find discrepancies in the debt records — payments made but never credited. POV: Sebastian. Beat: hope with teeth; they realize someone falsified the ledger.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Following the paper trail, Elodie and Sebastian discover the loan documents bear a signature dated while Sebastian's father was already hospitalized — forged, likely by someone inside the family business. POV: Elodie. Suspicion falls on the loyal estate manager, Henri. Beat: betrayal inside the walls; justice begins to matter more than love.

chapters.title: Henri's Confession
chapters.summary: Confronted, elderly Henri admits he altered records — but only to hide payments his late master ordered diverted to Camille's father, settling an older, unspoken debt between the two families. POV: Henri (via Elodie's recorded interview). Beat: the past is more tangled than anyone knew; two feuds, one root.

chapters.title: What Camille Is Owed
chapters.summary: Sebastian drives to Roux estate to confront Camille directly. She confesses her bank pressure is personal: her father died believing the Almeidas cheated him, and she inherited the grudge along with the loans. POV: Sebastian. Beat: enemy revealed as fellow mourner; hatred loses its footing.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Camille offers a deal: she'll restructure the loan if Sebastian publicly acknowledges his father's wrongdoing at the harvest festival. His name, his legacy, his pride — the price of the land. POV: Sebastian. He refuses; Elodie argues honor isn't a lie you keep. First real fight between the lovers. Beat: love against duty, both directions.

chapters.title: The Photograph Elodie Never Took
chapters.summary: Sorting the final archive boxes, Elodie finds letters proving Sebastian's father diverted funds to save Camille's father from prison — a sacrifice disguised as theft. POV: Elodie. The truth reframes everything: the elder Almeida took the shame so another family could survive. Beat: devastating tenderness; the dead were kinder than the living believed.

chapters.title: Veraison
chapters.summary: The grapes begin to ripen. Elodie shows Sebastian the letters; he weeps over his father's handwriting for the first time since the funeral. POV: Sebastian. They decide together: the truth will come out at the festival, whatever it costs. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the couple fully united.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Night
chapters.summary: Someone releases the cellar's fermentation tanks days before the festival — years of wine destroyed. Evidence points to a desperate creditor, not Camille, whose own crop was also hit. POV: Elodie. Beat: crisis peak; the vineyard may not survive to see its vindication.

chapters.title: Rivals in the Ruins
chapters.summary: Camille arrives at dawn — not gloating but offering her own reserve stock to blend for the festival tasting. Two rival houses, one table, all hands working. POV: Camille. Beat: the thaw; rivalry dissolving into something like sisterhood over shared loss.

chapters.title: The Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Before the whole valley, Sebastian tells the truth: his father's crime, his father's sacrifice, the forged ledgers meant to bury both. He offers the vineyard to a grower's cooperative rather than let either family own the grievance alone. POV: Sebastian. Beat: climax; justice outside the law, spoken aloud, costing everything and freeing everyone.

chapters.title: Signatures
chapters.summary: Camille tears up the foreclosure order and countersigns the cooperative charter. The crowd — workers, rivals, creditors — raises glasses of the blended rescue vintage. POV: Elodie. Watching Sebastian laugh freely for the first time, she understands what staying means. Beat: release; the community becomes the inheritance.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Quiet epilogue-of-sorts: the station platform, empty tracks, Elodie's Lyon apartment sublet to a stranger. She and Sebastian walk home through the rows, planning a winter of restoring the archive together — every photograph, every letter, nothing thrown away. POV: Elodie. Beat: peace chosen daily, not won once.

chapters.title: First Light on the Vines
chapters.summary: One year later: the cooperative's second harvest, Elodie's exhibition of restored Almeida photographs hanging in the cellar, Camille pouring beside Sebastian. Elodie hangs the final frame — the photo of her at twenty-four, now joined by a new one taken this morning. POV: Elodie. Final beat: love kept in the present tense, where it belongs.
